keyWhy.ko: 핵심은 «하얀 토끼가 달빛을 타고 내려온다(사건)» 와 «지우가 매일 밤 달토끼에게 손을 흔든다(결말)» 입니다. 초록색 문장이 정답이에요.
keyWhy.en: The key ideas are the event (a white rabbit jumps down on a moonbeam) and the ending (Jiwoo waves to the Moon rabbit every night). The green sentences are the answers.

boxes.a: Jiwoo, Grandma, and the Moon rabbit
A white rabbit jumps down from the Moon on a moonbeam.
They eat rice cakes together, and now Jiwoo waves to the rabbit every night.

sumHowto.en: Look at the three boxes, then choose the right word for each blank.

words: Grandma says a rabbit lives on the Moon.
a small animal with long ears
"It makes rice cakes all night," she says.
soft, sweet Korean food made from rice
Suddenly, a white rabbit jumps down on a moonbeam!
a line of light from the Moon
Then the rabbit hops back up to the Moon.
Now Jiwoo waves to the Moon rabbit every night.
moves a hand to say hello or goodbye

qs.q: Why does Jiwoo like the rice cake?
evs: Grandma says a rabbit lives on the Moon.
That night, Jiwoo looks at the full Moon.
Jiwoo takes one. It is sweet and soft.
Then the rabbit hops back up to the Moon.
why: 떡이 «sweet and soft», 달콤하고 말랑해서 좋아요.
The rice cake is sweet and soft, so Jiwoo likes it.

qs.q: "They eat rice cakes and talk until the sky gets light." What does "until the sky gets light" mean?
qs.qko: «until the sky gets light» 는 무슨 뜻일까요?
evs: "It makes rice cakes all night," she says.
They eat rice cakes and talk until the sky gets light.
"Would you like a rice cake?" it asks.
Now Jiwoo waves to the Moon rabbit every night.
why: «the sky gets light» 는 하늘이 밝아진다는 뜻이에요. 밤새 이야기하다가 아침이 될 때까지라는 말이에요.
"The sky gets light" means the morning comes. They talk all night until morning.

qs.q: How do we know Grandma's story is true?
qs.qko: 할머니 이야기가 진짜라는 것을 어떻게 알 수 있나요?
opts: Grandma shows Jiwoo a photo of the Moon.
Jiwoo flies to the Moon in a rocket.
A rabbit comes down and gives Jiwoo a rice cake.
evs: "It makes rice cakes all night," she says.
That night, Jiwoo looks at the full Moon.
Then the rabbit hops back up to the Moon.
"Would you like a rice cake?" it asks.
why: 할머니는 토끼가 떡을 만든다고 했어요(«It makes rice cakes...»). 정말로 토끼가 «떡 먹을래?» 하고 물어요. 두 문장을 이어야 알 수 있어요.
Grandma says the rabbit makes rice cakes, and the rabbit really offers Jiwoo a rice cake. You need both sentences.

ends: Jiwoo visits the Moon and helps the rabbit make rice cakes.
지우가 달에 가서 토끼와 함께 떡을 만든다.
Jiwoo makes a rice cake for the Moon rabbit.
A Gift for the Moon Rabbit

write.src: “I want to <u>meet the Moon rabbit</u> because <u>it makes sweet rice cakes</u>.”
write.howtoKo: 예문을 틀로 삼아, 빈칸 두 곳을 «하고 싶은 일 + 그 이유» 로 바꿔 영어로 써 보세요.
write.howtoEn: Use the example as a pattern. Write what you want to do and your reason in English.
write.moreKo: 한 걸음 더: «because» 뒤에 «누가 + 무엇을» 넣어 이유를 분명하게 써 보세요. (예: because my friends like it)
write.moreEn: One more step: after «because», write who + what to make your reason clear. (e.g. because my friends like it)

img.cover: On a quiet night under a huge full Moon, a small fluffy white rabbit with long ears, pink cheeks and a tiny blue scarf slides down a glowing silver moonbeam toward a garden, and Jiwoo, a girl with two short black braids, wearing yellow pajamas with white stars, looks up from the garden with wide, happy eyes.

scenes.1: In a moonlit garden, a small fluffy white rabbit with long ears, pink cheeks and a tiny blue scarf holds out a plate of round white rice cakes, and Jiwoo, a girl with two short black braids, wearing yellow pajamas with white stars, reaches out to take one with a big smile.
scenes.2: As the sky turns pink at dawn, a small fluffy white rabbit with long ears, pink cheeks and a tiny blue scarf hops up a fading moonbeam toward the pale Moon, and Jiwoo, a girl with two short black braids, wearing yellow pajamas with white stars, waves goodbye from the garden.
